wu: Travel Bingo: Students draw 4 travel words on a grid. Teacher calls out words (e.g., 'hotel', 'reservation', 'passport'). Students cross off matches and shout 'Bingo!' when complete.
wuAlt: Travel Pictionary: Teacher writes words on slips (e.g., 'suitcase', 'check-in'). Students draw while others guess.
Travel Charades: Students act out travel actions (e.g., 'boarding a plane') for others to name.
pres: Show flashcards of hotel items (key, room number, reception). Model: 'I have a reservation.' 'My name is...' 'I need a room.' Check understanding by asking: 'What do you say at a hotel?'
presAlt: Roleplay demo: Teacher acts as receptionist, student as guest. Use a toy phone and a fake registration form.
Realia: Display a hotel key and brochure. Point to items while modeling sentences.
prac: Pair drill: Student A is receptionist, Student B is guest. They practice 'I have a reservation' and 'My name is...' with cue cards (e.g., 'Smith', 'double room'). Teacher monitors and corrects pronunciation.
pracAlt: Chain game: Students pass a toy phone, saying 'I have a reservation for...' and adding a new word each time.
Gap-fill worksheet: Complete sentences like 'I have a ______ for two nights.' with options (reservation, ticket, passport).
ls: Listen to a hotel check-in dialogue. Students tick details heard (name, room type, nights). Play twice. Check answers as a class.
re: Stand up, Sit down: Teacher calls out travel words. Students stand if they match 'hotel' or 'reservation', sit for others. Quick review after break.
prod: Travel buddy interviews: Students ask partners about their dream holiday. Use prompts: 'Where do you want to go?' 'What kind of room do you need?' Share 2 findings with the class.
rw: Read a short hotel confirmation email. Circle the correct details (name: Ali/Amal, nights: 1/2). Then write 1 sentence: 'My name is...' using the email info.
st: Sing 'The Travel Song' (tune of 'Twinkle Twinkle') with actions. Close with: 'Today we learned hotel phrases. Thank you, class.'
g: Students mark off hotel words called by the teacher.
Teams race to write 'I have a reservation' on the board.
Match cards with room numbers to guest names.
Act out travel words for others to guess.
Pass a box while music plays; say a travel word when it stops.
diff: Fast finishers: Write 3 more sentences about their ideal hotel.
Support: Use sentence starters like 'My name is...' for the roleplay.
hw: Practice the hotel roleplay with a family member.
Write 3 questions you would ask at a hotel check-in.
Draw a picture of your dream hotel and label 2 items (bed, pool).
tip: Use Moroccan travel examples (e.g., booking a hotel for Agadir or Marrakech) to make it relevant. Pair adults with similar life experiences for roleplays.
